statement: Samsung co-led a EUR 200 million (about $231 million) Series A for Dutch startup Euclyd, which is building a non-GPU AI inference chip and memory architecture.
why: Capital flowing into alternative inference silicon backed by a major memory maker is an early marker of future competition for merchant GPU inference sockets.

impact.mechanism: Funding plus Samsung's memory manufacturing and supply-chain support moves an alternative inference architecture toward production, adding potential non-GPU supply.

evidence.excerpt: designing an AI chip system, with different architecture to GPUs, for inference, including the processor and memory architecture,

confidence.basis: Single secondary aggregator source; funding is confirmed but the product is pre-silicon.

dispersion: conflicting same-key reports: statement/trend changed (trend rising -> rising); sources: gate.com
